channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Indonesia to Review Staff Rotations Linked to Finance Chief Swap
item.description: Indonesia’s Finance Ministry is reviewing a surprise reshuffle of hundreds of staff that former minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa said helped trigger his dismissal.
item.dc:creator: Norman Harsono

item.title: Australia to Target Family Visas, Overstayers to Curb Migration
item.description: Australia’s center-left government is set to outline plans to reduce immigration on Thursday, including a clampdown on people who have overstayed their visas and restricting most people on student visas from bringing family into the country.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: Russia Taps North Korean Workers to Make Drones Under Fake Visas
item.description: Russia is increasingly mobilizing North Korean workers to build military drones for use against Ukraine in defiance of international sanctions, giving Pyongyang a key source of revenue to fund its unlawful weapons programs, the US and its allies said in a report.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Trump Returns to Trail in North Carolina With Senate in Play
item.description: President Donald Trump visited North Carolina in his first campaign stop since the GOP’s Dallas midterm convention, seeking to boost Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley, who is trailing Democrat Roy Cooper in the polls.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Thai Protest Leader Who Seized Bangkok Airport Is Back in Action
item.description: A Thai protest leader whose mass demonstrations nearly 20 years ago closed the capital’s airports and helped oust governments is now focused on Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, and aims to build a political force capable of outlasting him.
item.dc:creator: Randy Thanthong-Knight and Patpicha Tanakasempipat

item.title: Trump Floats EU Tariffs If Canada Invite Deemed Hostile Act
item.description: President Donald Trump floated hitting goods imported from the European Union with fresh tariffs or even cutting off some trade if he determined that a push to make Canada a potential associate of the bloc was harmful to the US.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Jeff Mason

item.title: Warsh Declines Comment on Any Discussion With President Trump
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Reps. Mike Lawler (R-NY) and Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) say they would not have raised interest rates and discuss the impact of higher rates and inflation on consumers. In a Truth Social post, Trump said that US rates “should be 1%, or less." Chris Phelan, White House Council of Economic Advisers chairman, agrees and says anyway you measure it - inflation is coming down. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Businessweek Daily: The Fed Raises Rates (Podcast)
item.description:
The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by a quarter percentage point and penciled in an additional hike later this year, steps aimed at containing inflation that will test Chairman Kevin Warsh’s relationship with President Donald Trump. Following the US central bank’s first rate increase since July 2023, Warsh restated his concerns over inflation, saying too many categories of products and services were showing annualized price gains above 3% on a 6- and 12-month basis.
On today's episode:
Michael McKee, Bloomberg News International Economics & Policy Correspondent Stephanie Aliaga, Global Market Strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management Manju Boraiah, Head of Systematic Fixed Income & Custom SMA Portfolio Management at Allspring Global Investments Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal, Co-Hosts of Bloomberg's Odd Lots Podcast (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran Blockade Is Draining US Military's Global Power
item.description: Bloomberg's Becca Wasser and Courtney McBride joined the show to discuss their latest reporting on the cost of the US naval blockade of Iran and how the deployment is straining military readiness and resources. They speak with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: House Passes Bill Allowing New Tariffs on Russia Oil Buyers
item.description: Congress gave final approval to a bill to give President Donald Trump new powers to impose tariffs on countries that purchase Russian petroleum products, a setback for a coalition of business lobbyists concerned the legislation creates a legal underpinning for a broad new tariff regime against US trading partners.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson and Caitlin Reilly

item.title: Reps. Lawler and Gottheimer Speak on Fed Rate Decision, AI Bill
item.description: Reps. Mike Lawler (R-NY) and Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) say they would not have raised interest rates and discuss the impact of higher rates and inflation on consumers. Rep. Lawler says the Fed’s decision demonstrated its independence and discusses President Trump’s proposed $5,000 dividend and questions over how it would be paid for. Rep. Gottheimer says higher rates will hurt consumers through credit-card bills, housing payments and other costs. They also discuss their bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act and the need for federal standards to identify and control AI agents, while keeping the US competitive in artificial intelligence. They speak with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Calls Fed Rate Hike 'Unfortunate,' Demands a Cut
item.description: President Donald Trump says the Fed was wrong to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point. In a Truth Social post, Trump said that US rates “should be 1%, or less." Chris Phelan, White House Council of Economic Advisers chairman, agrees and says anyway you measure it - inflation is coming down. He is on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Le Pen Leaves Door Open to No-Confidence Vote Over 2027 Budget
item.description: Marine Le Pen, the French far-right leader and presidential candidate, kept open the possibility of censuring the government over the 2027 budget, while at the same time pledging not to take action that could damage the country’s strained finances.
item.dc:creator: Nayla Razzouk

item.title: Rouse: Have Not Seen Full AI Productivity Impact
item.description: Brookings President Cecilia Rouse discusses the human impact of the Fed’s decision, emphasizing that monetary policy affects paychecks, hiring, borrowing costs, and retirement planning—not just basis points and forecasts. She says the Fed is trying to restore price stability while avoiding a deeper downturn in the labor market. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Exxon Is in Talks to Return to Venezuela as Deals Accelerate
item.description: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. held talks this week with Venezuela’s government about re-entering the country as the Texas oil giant explores whether to follow US rivals back into the home of the world’s largest reserves.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Crowley, Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Ari Natter and Eric Martin

item.title: Trump Backs Warsh, Faults ‘Hostile’ Fed Board for Rate Hike
item.description: President Donald Trump said he still had confidence in Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh and criticized what he said was a “hostile” board even after the central bank unanimously defied his calls to lower borrowing costs.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse, Hadriana Lowenkron and Jeff Mason

item.title: Midterms Pit Republican Cash Machine Against Democratic Fury
item.description: Money may talk, but the discontents of voters ring loud
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: House Holds Leon Black in Contempt in Epstein Subpoena Clash
item.description: The US House voted to hold billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress for failure to comply with two subpoenas issued in a committee’s investigation into sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: China Considers BYD for Xi’s CEO Entourage at Trump Summit
item.description: Chinese officials are considering BYD Co. for a possible business delegation joining Xi Jinping’s summit with Donald Trump next week in Washington, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Indian and Pakistani Warships Collide at Sea, Refueling Tensions
item.description: India and Pakistan traded blame on Wednesday over a collision between their warships at sea, adding a new point of friction between the arch rivals and nuclear-armed neighbors.
item.dc:creator: Sudhi Ranjan Sen and Tooba Khan
